title: B-tree, hash, GIN, GiST and BRIN: the index for the question

videos.script: Lesson 2 found the most expensive query in the workload: a search by tag on products. {{tally}} It asks for products whose tags contain a word, and it reads all fifty thousand rows to find them. {{seqscan}} The obvious fix is an index. The question is which one. {{which}} A B-tree, the index you already know, keeps values in order. It answers equals, less than, between and order by. It cannot answer contains. {{btree}} PostgreSQL has other structures, and each one answers a different kind of question. A hash index answers only equals, and is smaller for it. GIN looks inside a value: the elements of an array, the keys of a JSON document. GiST answers is near and overlaps. BRIN keeps one small summary for each stretch of the table, and is tiny, as long as the table is in order. {{five}} In this lesson you build each of them on market, measure its size, and watch the question it answers. {{market}} And the tag search gets two indexes. The first is the one the textbook names. The second is faster still, because it answers the other half of the question. {{halves}}
